Projects

AI lead conversion system for a renovation company

Simulated client. Built with n8n, Gemini, HubSpot and Mailpit, all free tools.

A renovation business loses jobs when homeowners wait a day for an answer. I built a system that scores each web-form inquiry, saves it to the CRM, alerts the owner to the good ones, answers the rest, and holds back any reply it is not sure about.

Tested on 30 labelled fake leadsResult
Category correct, all leads27 of 30
Category correct, clear leads27 of 27
Spam caught4 of 4
Prompt-injection attemptResisted
Failed AI calls0

The three misses were borderline-area leads in Barrie, Guelph and Niagara Falls. The system flagged each one as uncertain and sent it to the owner instead of replying.

How a lead moves through it
  1. Form. The homeowner describes the project.
  2. Clean. Fields are tidied into one standard format.
  3. Classify. An AI model returns hot, warm, cold or spam, a score, a reason and a draft reply.
  4. Route. Fixed rules decide the path, so behaviour stays predictable.
  5. Save. The CRM gets the contact, once, with the AI’s findings.
  6. Act. Hot leads go to the owner. Others get a reply only if confidence and service-area checks pass.
  7. Watch. Failures trigger an email, so no lead disappears quietly.
What testing caught

A reply invented a company policy. A draft told a lead the business avoids small repairs, which nobody had said. I added a fact sheet of real services and a rule to say “I’m not sure” about anything unlisted.

The AI was fully confident about vague leads. A confidence threshold alone would have caught almost nothing, so I put plain rule-based checks behind it.

Free-tier limits broke my first test run. Most calls failed at five requests a minute. I throttled the test, moved to a stable model, and tested the same model I deploy.

AI sales dashboard with checked insights

Portfolio project. Built with Python, Pandas, Plotly, Streamlit, Gemini and Supabase.

Small businesses often keep their sales in a spreadsheet and never get answers out of it. I built a web app where you upload a CSV or Excel file and get a clean dashboard, interactive charts and a short plain-language summary written by an AI.

Python calculates every number. The AI only explains them, and the app checks every figure in the AI’s text against the calculated ones before showing it.

Checked on two sample shopsResult
Clean file, rows used14 of 14
Messy file, bad rows left out3 of 17
Messy file, column names matched5 of 5
Automated tests10 passing
AI figures checked against PythonEvery one

The messy file uses different column names and has an empty quantity, a price marked “N/A” and a date that was never recorded. The app matches the columns, leaves out the unusable rows and tells the user how many it dropped. Both sample files are in the code repository, so anyone can try them on the live demo.

How a file moves through it
  1. Upload. A CSV or Excel file, or the built-in sample data.
  2. Check. The app looks for the five columns it needs and offers a drop-down match when the names differ.
  3. Clean. Rows with missing or invalid values are left out, and the user is told how many.
  4. Calculate. Python works out revenue, totals, the best product and the best city.
  5. Show. Summary cards, interactive charts and a data table, laid out for phones as well as desktops.
  6. Explain. Signed-in users can ask an AI for a short summary. It receives only the totals, never the full file.
  7. Verify. Every number in the AI’s text is compared with the calculated ones, and a mismatch shows a warning.
  8. Keep. Reports can be downloaded or saved to a private history, where each user sees only their own.
What testing caught

Data from the previous user stayed on screen. After one test account logged out and another logged in, the first account’s uploaded file was still showing. Saved reports were already private, but the page was not cleared. Logging out now wipes it.

The login was hidden on phones. The sign-in form sat in a side menu that phones fold away behind a small arrow. I moved the account, upload and report controls onto the main page.

An AI model was retired. The first AI call failed because Google had replaced the model I picked. The app now shows a clear message instead of crashing, and I updated the model name.

AI business operations app for small teams

Portfolio project. Built with Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Gemini, GitHub Actions, n8n and Render, all on free tiers.

A small business loses customers when enquiries sit unanswered. I built Lumen, a web app that sorts each incoming enquiry, hands it to the right person, drafts a reminder when one goes quiet, and answers staff questions from the business’s own saved notes.

The AI never contacts a customer on its own. A person reviews every draft, and when the AI cannot decide how to sort something, the app flags it for a person instead of guessing.

How it is set upResult
Automated tests27
Stale enquiry gets a draft reminder after2 days
AI calls per plan, Free and Pro50 and 500
Daily follow-up check09:00 Lagos
Demo sandbox is cleared after24 hours

The tests cover login, permissions, data isolation between businesses, sorting, plans, usage limits and demo mode. The demo is a private sandbox with sample data, so anyone can try every screen without signing up.

How an enquiry moves through it
  1. Arrive. A new enquiry is added to the business’s inbox.
  2. Sort. An AI model gives it a category and a priority. If it cannot decide, the enquiry is flagged “needs sorting”.
  3. Assign. It goes to a team member. When an owner assigns it by hand, the flag clears.
  4. Wait. If nothing happens for 2 days, the app asks the AI for a friendly draft reminder.
  5. Review. A person reads the draft, copies it and marks it done. Nothing is sent automatically.
  6. Notify. A scheduled job runs every morning and sends a Telegram message to the owner when new reminders exist.
  7. Answer. Staff can ask questions and get replies drawn only from saved notes, with the source note shown. If the notes do not say, the app says so.
Design choices and known limits

One business can never see another’s data. Every database query is filtered by the business, and isolation tests guard each endpoint.

Plan limits are enforced on the server. The buttons only hide options, and the API refuses the rest. AI calls are counted before they are made.

There is no payment behind the plan switch. Any owner can move to Pro. A real product would put a payment provider in front of it.

Free hosting sleeps. The first visit after a quiet period can take about a minute to wake up.

About

My journey into Software Engineering began in growth strategy, where I worked on helping businesses attract customers, improve performance, and grow.

Along the way, I encountered projects where things weren’t working as they should. Processes were becoming difficult to manage, tasks weren’t flowing efficiently, and operational inefficiencies were limiting business performance.

That experience changed how I looked at technology.

I realised that helping a business grow isn’t just about acquiring more customers. It’s also about building the software, systems, and infrastructure that enable businesses to operate efficiently, solve problems, and scale without unnecessary complexity.

That’s what led me into Software Engineering.

Today, I focus on designing and building software solutions that combine programming, artificial intelligence, and business process automation to solve practical problems.

My work revolves around

  1. Software Development: Building applications, backend systems, APIs, and digital solutions that address real-world business challenges.
  2. AI Integration: Incorporating AI and large language models into applications to improve decision-making, productivity, and business operations.
  3. Business Process Automation: Designing intelligent workflows that eliminate repetitive tasks and reduce manual operations.
  4. System Integration: Connecting applications, databases, APIs, and business tools to create efficient, interconnected systems.
  5. Data Analytics: Transforming business data into actionable insights that support better decisions.

My technical toolkit

  • Languages: Python, JavaScript
  • Backend: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy
  • Databases: PostgreSQL, Supabase, Neon
  • AI: Gemini, LLM API integration
  • Data: Pandas, Plotly
  • Automation: n8n, GitHub Actions
  • Deployment: Docker, Render

My approach to software development goes beyond writing code or introducing new technologies. It starts with understanding a problem, designing an appropriate solution, building the system, and ensuring it delivers practical value.

I believe technology should make businesses more capable, not more complicated.

Whether it’s developing a custom application, integrating AI into an existing system, or automating complex workflows, my goal is to turn ideas and business challenges into functional, scalable software solutions.

I’m particularly interested in collaborating with businesses, startups, and teams building technology-driven solutions.

Let’s build something meaningful.
